title: Viradha
hook: the giant falls, and at the edge of a freshly dug pit he suddenly remembers who he used to be

segments.voice: Yesterday: Viradha, the giant no weapon can kill. He seized Sita and carried off the brothers, until they broke his arms.

Here's the problem. Viradha is down, arms broken, but no weapon can kill him. Brahma's boon still holds. So what do you do with an enemy who can't die the ordinary way? Rama tells Lakshmana to dig a pit, a deep one, big enough for a body that size. While Lakshmana digs, Rama puts his foot on Viradha's throat to hold him down. That's when the giant's face changes.
screen: `AN ENEMY WHO CAN'T DIE.` → `DIG A PIT.` → `THE GIANT'S FACE CHANGES.`

segments.voice: Viradha looks up and recognizes him. You're Rama, Kausalya's son. I was told you would come. Then he tells his story. He wasn't always a forest giant. He was a gandharva, one of the celestial musicians, named Tumburu, who served Kubera, the lord of wealth. But he fell in love with Rambha, one of the apsaras, and in his longing he neglected his duty and didn't show up when he should have. Kubera cursed him: become a rakshasa, a terror of the forest. Tumburu begged for mercy, and Kubera set a limit. When Rama, son of Dasharatha, kills you in battle, you'll be released and return to heaven. So through all those years of being monstrous, Viradha was waiting for this. He even tells them how to finish it. Bury me; it's the way for one like me. And one more thing: a few miles from here lives a great sage, Sharabhanga. Go to him. He'll help you. So the brothers lower him into the pit, and as the earth covers him, Viradha leaves the body and rises, released. Yesterday he was the forest's first monster. Today he's a cursed musician who was waiting to be set free. The Ramayana does this again and again: under a terrifying face, a story, a curse and a release. The enemy becomes the guide who points the way.
screen: `YOU'RE RAMA. I WAS TOLD YOU'D COME.` · `TUMBURU, A CURSED MUSICIAN.` · `BURY ME. GO TO SHARABHANGA.` · `RISING, RELEASED.` · then, large: `THE ENEMY BECOMES THE GUIDE.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind someone who frightened or frustrated you this year, and hold them lightly, at a distance. Without inventing anything or excusing anything, leave room for a story under their behavior that you don't know, and breathe until the picture softens a little.
Viradha. A gandharva named Tumburu, cursed to be a giant until Rama came. Buried, he rises free, and sends Rama to Sharabhanga.
Your line: the enemy becomes the guide. Under the monster was a musician. Day five hundred fifty-four.

howItsDone: Hindu storytellers often point to Viradha as the first of several beings in the Ramayana released from a curse by meeting Rama, a pattern many devotees read as a sign of his grace.

chat.says: Was Viradha just a monster that Rama killed?

chat.meaning: Viradha was Tumburu, a gandharva cursed by Kubera to be a rakshasa until Rama came. Buried, he rose released and sent Rama to Sharabhanga.

Tumburu.meaning: the gandharva Viradha had been before the curse

Kubera.meaning: the lord of wealth, who cursed Tumburu

Rambha.meaning: an apsara, one of heaven's dancers

rakshasa.meaning: a demon of the epics, a terror of the forest
